description:
A driver in Sarajevo takes one wrong turn on a sunny morning, stalls the car outside a sandwich shop, and twenty million people die in World War I. What if your entire life isn't a neat story of merit and planning, but an unbroken chain of flukes?

That's the radical premise of "Fluke: Chance, Chaos, and Why Everything We Do Matters" by Brian Klaas — and it completely dismantles the way we think about success, planning, and control.

In this comprehensive deep dive, we explore why human beings suffer from the tyranny of linear causality: we convince ourselves that effort cleanly dictates outcome, when in reality we live in a coupled, sensitive, chaotic system where microscopic accidents constantly dictate the course of history and our personal lives.
